Hallo,

es war viel los im Repo und daher der Vorschlag ein Changelog.md anzulegen.

Das wäre der Vorschlag für die Änderungen von Anfang an bis Heute:

---

# BSI Stand-der-Technik-Bibliothek — Change Report

**Repository:** [BSI-Bund/Stand-der-Technik-Bibliothek](https://github.com/BSI-Bund/Stand-der-Technik-Bibliothek)
**Period covered:** full history — 2025-09-15 (initial commit) to 2026-08-01, with focus on the last 5 months
**Report date:** 2026-08-01
**Activity:** 60 commits on `main` in total, 30 of them since March 2026 (main contributors: Raphael Miether, Leon Wagner, Dario Friedsam, Liam Herring; community PRs from Daniel Ruf, LeonKohli, Sönke von Repel; plus a new `rolling-publication-bot`)

---

## Executive summary

Since its launch in September 2025 the library has evolved in three architectural generations — `Kompendien/` (Sep 2025), `Anwenderkataloge/`+`Quellkataloge/` (Jan 2026), and the current three-layer structure (Jul 2026) — while the data model was translated to English and enriched semantically. In the last five months, five developments stand out:

1. **Full repository restructure (2026-07-27)** into three layers — `control_layer/`, `implementation_layer/`, `assessment_layer/` — breaking every previously published path.
2. **Automated rolling publication** (late July): a bot now publishes generated artifacts via CI, replacing hand-committed "Update" drops.
3. **Authoritative security-target and threat metadata (2026-07-03)**: every control now carries confidentiality/integrity/availability/authenticity ratings (0–2) and mappings to the elementary threats (elementare Gefährdungen).
4. **New catalogs and mappings (2026-07-17)**: Lieferkettensicherheit (supply-chain security), WLAN, ISO 27001 Annex A mapping, and an IT-Grundschutz-2023-to-G++ mapping.
5. **Continued anglicization** of the OSCAL data model (props, namespace files, folder names), begun in March.

The Grundschutz++ user catalog stands at **20 groups / 1,000 controls** (994 in March), resolved from the Kernel catalog (901 controls), the Methodik-Grundschutz++ catalog, and the new risk-management source catalog.

---

## Timeline of changes

### Phase 0: September 2025 – February 2026 — From "Kompendium" to catalog structure

The repository launched on **2025-09-15** with a very different shape than today. Understanding this phase explains several of the later renames.

- **2025-09-15** (`16701d4`): **Initial commit** (27 files, ~109,000 lines). The library consisted of:
  - `Kompendien/Grundschutz++-Kompendium/` — the G++ compendium as **both JSON and XML**,
  - `Quellkataloge/Kernel/` and `Quellkataloge/Grundschutz++-Methodik/` — the two source catalogs, plus `grundschutz-gesamt-oscal-profile.json`,
  - `Dokumentation/namespaces/` with **all-German CSV names** (`modalverb.csv`, `handlungsworte.csv`, `praktiken.csv`, `sicherheitsniveau.csv`, `abhängigkeit.txt`, …),
  - CONTRIBUTING.md and CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md.
- **October 2025 — first community contributions.** The repo drew immediate external attention:
  - Daniel Ruf: wording/typo fixes — PR #4: https://github.com/BSI-Bund/Stand-der-Technik-Bibliothek/pull/4, PR #5: https://github.com/BSI-Bund/Stand-der-Technik-Bibliothek/pull/5, PR #8: https://github.com/BSI-Bund/Stand-der-Technik-Bibliothek/pull/8
  - Sönke von Repel: numbering fix in Monitoring/Evaluation — PR #9: https://github.com/BSI-Bund/Stand-der-Technik-Bibliothek/pull/9
  - LeonKohli: **namespace-URL and filename corrections** across all three main artifacts, ~12,700 lines — PR #19: https://github.com/BSI-Bund/Stand-der-Technik-Bibliothek/pull/19
  - broken Kompendium XML repaired — PR #25: https://github.com/BSI-Bund/Stand-der-Technik-Bibliothek/pull/25
  - **2025-10-15** (`4612be8`): first data-model formalization — `oscal_satzschablone_schema.json` (sentence-template schema) and the namespaces `readme.md` added, all namespace CSVs reworked.
- **November 2025:** README/CONTRIBUTING clarifications (including a commit by "Christoph" on 2025-11-13) and a catalog/namespace refresh (`3913b4b`).
- **2025-12-05** (`f52d4c0`): **XML format dropped** — the Kompendium became JSON-only. From here on the library is a pure OSCAL-JSON publication.
- **2025-12-18** (`9dbd537`): largest catalog rework of the early phase (~62,800 insertions / 48,800 deletions across Kompendium, Kernel and Methodik).
- **2026-01-20** (`313e2bd`): **"Kompendium" concept retired.** `Kompendien/Grundschutz++-Kompendium/Grundschutz++-Kompendium.json` became `Anwenderkataloge/Grundschutz++/Grundschutz++-catalog.json` — the user-catalog (Anwenderkatalog) structure that held until the July 2026 layer restructure.
- **2026-01-29** (`30daef3`, `352e086`): profile mechanics cleaned up — `grundschutz-gesamt-oscal-profile.json` replaced by `Grundschutz++-profile.json`; the Methodik catalog renamed to `BSI-Methodik-Grundschutz++` and moved to `Quellkataloge/Methodik-Grundschutz++/`.
- **February 2026** (`28baaac`, `ee65e9d`): two consolidation rounds on catalogs, Handlungsworte, Themen and Dokumentationsempfehlungen — the last commits before the anglicization push.

**Naming lineage of the central artifact:** `Grundschutz++-Kompendium.json` (Sep 2025) → `Grundschutz++-catalog.json` (Jan 2026) → `Grundschutz++-resolved_catalog.json` (Jul 2026).

### March 2026 — English data model begins

- **2026-03-05** (`ee5e510`): Namespace housekeeping — `stufen.csv` → `aufwand.csv`, `zielobjekte.csv` → `zielobjektkategorien.csv` ("target objects" became "target object *categories*"), catalog refresh.
- **2026-03-16** (`9bae4ad`): **Systematic English conversion** of OSCAL props and namespace files (~22,000 lines touched, including `oscal_satzschablone_schema.json`). The exact prop renames on every control:

  | Old prop name | New prop name | Count |
  |---|---|---|
  | `modalverb` | `modal_verb` | 994 |
  | `handlungsworte` | `action_word` | 994 |
  | `ergebnis` | `result` | 994 |
  | `präzisierung` | `result_specification` | 444 |
  | `target_objects` | `target_object_categories` | 620 |

  Unchanged props: `statement`, `sec_level`, `effort_level`, `guidance`, `documentation`, `tags`, `label`, `alt-identifier`. Namespace file renames: `handlungsworte.csv` → `action_words.csv`, `modalverb.csv` → `modal_verbs.csv`, `aufwand.csv` → `effort_level.csv`, `abhängigkeit.txt` → `dependency.txt`, `sicherheitsniveau.csv` → `security_level.csv` (values `normal-SdT` / `erhöht`), `dokumentationsempfehlungen.csv` → `documentation_guidelines.csv`, `verbesserung.txt` → `enhancement.txt`. **Any consumer matching props by name or resolving ns URIs broke here** — the first of two big breaking changes in the period.

### April 2026 — Risk management, first components, TLS draft

- **2026-04-02** (`780aa77`): New source catalog **BSI-Anforderungen-zum-Risikomanagement** with 10 requirements, RISK.1.1–RISK.1.10: Methodik für das Risikomanagement, Einhaltung der BSI-Kriterien, Risikoeigentümer, Risikoappetit, Freigabe des Risikomanagements, Kritikalitätskriterien für Geschäftsprozesse, Kriterien für die Risikobeurteilung, Kriterien für die Risikoakzeptanz, Bestätigung des Restrisikos, Freigabe der Umsetzungsplanung. Four of them were integrated into the Grundschutz++ user catalog (994 → 998 controls). New namespace values added to `practices.csv`, `tags.csv`, `topics.csv`.
- **2026-04-20** (`67233f5`): **First OSCAL component definitions** under `Implementierungsbeschreibungen/Komponenten/`: AWS example components (IAM, Security Hub), **Netzarchitektur** (network architecture — the largest, mapping 85 G++ requirements to implementation statements), and **Passwortrichtlinie** (password policy, 17 requirements).
- **2026-04-21/23** (`f2577cf`, `17a8cfe`, `6dcbc0c`): **Mindeststandard TLS** catalog added (889 lines), withdrawn one day later, and re-published on 04-23 explicitly as a *draft* (`Entwurf-Mindeststandard-TLS-catalog.json`, 3 groups / 17 controls, 958 lines). It has not been touched since and remains the only artifact still on its April version.

### May–June 2026 — Consolidation

- **2026-05-13** (`0e32a81` + 2 reverted attempts): one-line wording fix in the definition of the target-object category *Mitarbeitende* — took Liam Herring three commits to land, suggesting manual editing without CI validation at the time.
- **2026-05-29** (`b4e1ee4`): small ID reshuffle (7 removed / 7 added): SENS.8 gained four sub-requirements (from GEB.10 and others); one requirement each moved within TEST.4, KONF.2, DET.3.
- **2026-06-08** (`41badd4`): substantial rework of the Passwortrichtlinie component (+330/−182 lines).
- **2026-06-23**: README updates (three commits, documentation only).
- **2026-06-30** (`313aa87`): **First big renumbering wave** (−5,409/+4,534 lines): **81 control IDs removed, 72 added** — a net −9, taking the catalog from 998 to 989 controls. This was not deletion of content but restructuring within groups: the entire **BER.7.x block (16 requirements + 6 sub-requirements) was renumbered to BER.6.x**, **STM.4–STM.9 collapsed into a new STM.2.1.x hierarchy**, **PERF.5/PERF.6 became PERF.3/PERF.4**, and GC sub-hierarchies (GC.6.1.x, GC.8.1.x) were re-nested (GC.8.1.1.1.1 → GC.9.1.1.1.x). KONF.11.8.x became KONF.11.7.x. Full ID lists in Appendix A. The same commit added two new action words to `action_words.csv`: **modellieren** and **analysieren** (with definitions distinguishing "analysieren" from "überprüfen"), and reworked `documentation_guidelines.csv`, `target_object_categories.csv`, `topics.csv`. The Methodik share of the G++ catalog shrank from 105 to 95 controls — the origin of the control-ID drift that hit downstream consumers (see "Impact").

### July 2026 — The big month

- **2026-07-03** (`d6153cb`, ~110,000 insertions): **Security targets and threat mappings** — the biggest *semantic* upgrade of the period:
  - Every Kernel-derived control (901 of the 1,000) gained four new props: **`confidentiality`, `integrity`, `availability`, `authenticity`**, each valued 0–2. Semantics (per `security_targets_levels.csv`, added 07-17): 0 = requirement has no/negligible effect on this protection goal, 1 = contributes to it, 2 = "the protection goal is the very center of this requirement".
  - Every Kernel control also gained a **`threats`** prop mapping it to the **47 elementare Gefährdungen** (G 0.1 Feuer … G 0.47), whose full texts were imported as `basethreats.csv` (469 lines, with UUIDs per threat). `security_targets.csv` defines the four protection goals with BSI-glossary definitions.
  - A new **Kernel-G0 catalog** (`BSI-Stand-der-Technik-Kernel-G0-catalog.json`, "Kernel + Gefährdungen") was introduced alongside the plain Kernel catalog — identical 14 groups / 901 controls, but carrying the threat/target annotations. The G++ resolved catalog switched its source class from `BSI-Stand-der-Technik-Kernel` to `BSI-Stand-der-Technik-Kernel-G0`.
  - Ten controls were added, mostly extending BER.3 (BER.3.26–BER.3.32, BER.3.1.1) plus BER.4.4.1/BER.4.9 (989 → 998). Notably, all of BER.3.26–32 were **removed again** in the July 29/30 renumbering — a churn cycle of under four weeks.
- **2026-07-17** (`12abb43`, ~97,000 insertions): Major artifact drop:
  - **Lieferkettensicherheit** (supply-chain security) catalog — 7 groups / **146 controls**, built as an OSCAL *profile* over the G++ sources (its groups reuse the G++ taxonomy: ASST Inventarisierung/Regelungen/Transfer/Wartung, BES Grundlagen through Lieferantenauswahl, DLS, etc.) with resolved catalog, profile, and a **component definition mapping all 145 requirements** to implementation statements.
  - **WLAN** catalog — 7 groups / **61 controls**, likewise a profile-based selection reusing G++ control IDs (ASST.2.2, ARCH.2.4–ARCH.3.x, KONF, DET …) plus WLAN-specific structuring.
  - **Mappings** (first of their kind in the repo): `ISO27001-AnnexA-catalog.json` (99 Annex-A controls as an OSCAL catalog) plus an **ISO 27001 Annex A → G++ mapping** with **96 mapping relationships**, and an **IT-Grundschutz Edition 2023 → G++ mapping** with **~1,185 relationship entries** — the machine-readable migration path from classic IT-Grundschutz to G++.
  - **GA-Lotse Grundmodul** component definition (draft — describes capabilities E-Mail, Kalender, Kontaktmanagement, but contains no control links yet).
- **2026-07-27** (`7ea2084`, PR #63: https://github.com/BSI-Bund/Stand-der-Technik-Bibliothek/pull/63): **Layer-based restructure.** 55 files moved/renamed:

  | Old path | New path |
  |---|---|
  | `Anwenderkataloge/Grundschutz++/Grundschutz++-catalog.json` | `control_layer/Grundschutz++/Grundschutz++-resolved_catalog.json` |
  | `Quellkataloge/Kernel/…`, `Quellkataloge/Methodik-Grundschutz++/…` | `control_layer/Grundschutz++/sources/catalogs/…` / `sources/profiles/…` |
  | `Quellkataloge/Risikomanagement/…` | `control_layer/Risikomanagement/…` |
  | `Mappings/…` | `control_layer/Mappings/…` (files renamed `*-mapping_collection.json`) |
  | `Implementierungsbeschreibungen/Komponenten/…` | `implementation_layer/…` |
  | `Dokumentation/…` | `documentation/…` (lowercase) |
  | — | `assessment_layer/` (new, README only — placeholder for assessment artifacts) |

  User catalogs were renamed `*-resolved_catalog.json`, signalling they are machine-resolved from profiles. READMEs per layer were added.
- **2026-07-28/30**: **Rolling publication automation.** New GitHub workflow `notify_internal_rolling_publication.yml`; a `rolling-publication-bot` now commits generated artifacts (PR #64: https://github.com/BSI-Bund/Stand-der-Technik-Bibliothek/pull/64, PR #65: https://github.com/BSI-Bund/Stand-der-Technik-Bibliothek/pull/65, PR #67: https://github.com/BSI-Bund/Stand-der-Technik-Bibliothek/pull/67). Through this channel:
  - **Second renumbering wave** (2026-07-29 build, published 07-30): 26 control IDs removed, 27 added — again entirely in **BER**. Remarkably, this wave **reintroduced the complete BER.7.x block** (BER.7.1–BER.7.16.6) that the June 30 wave had renumbered to BER.6.x, while removing the BER.3.26–3.32 and BER.6.7–6.16.x IDs. In other words, part of the June restructuring was reverted or reshuffled again within four weeks (full lists in Appendix A). Plus one deletion in SENS (SENS.7.25). Net result: 999 → **1,000 controls**.
  - New **Keycloak** component definition (43 implemented requirements, 2026-07-30).
  - Consolidated **AWS Security Hub** component (17 implemented requirements) replaced the two older AWS examples (`aws_iam`, `aws_security_hub`).
  - The obsolete WLAN component definition was removed.
  - `action_words.csv` normalization: all synonym lists converted from first-person forms to infinitives ("anordne, auferlege…" → "anordnen, auferlegen…") — relevant for anyone parsing the synonyms column.
  - All catalogs republished with fresh timestamps (2026-07-29 build); the metadata prop `resolution-tool` disappeared from the resolved catalog.

---

## Current state of the library (2026-08-01)

| Artifact | Scope | Size |
|---|---|---|
| Grundschutz++ resolved catalog | control_layer | 20 groups, **1,000 controls** |
| Kernel / Kernel-G0 source catalogs | control_layer (sources) | 14 groups, 901 controls |
| Risikomanagement catalog | control_layer | 10 controls |
| Lieferkettensicherheit resolved catalog | control_layer | 7 groups, 146 controls |
| WLAN resolved catalog | control_layer | 7 groups, 61 controls |
| Mindeststandard TLS (draft, stale since April) | control_layer | 3 groups, 17 controls |
| ISO 27001 Annex A catalog + mapping; IT-GS 2023 mapping | control_layer/Mappings | 2 mapping collections |
| Components: AWS Security Hub (17 reqs), GA-Lotse (draft, 0 reqs), Keycloak (43 reqs), Lieferkettensicherheit (145 reqs), Netzarchitektur (85 reqs), Passwortrichtlinie (17 reqs) | implementation_layer | 6 component definitions |
| Assessment layer | assessment_layer | placeholder only |

Composition of the 1,000 G++ controls: 900 Kernel-G0 + 95 Methodik-G++ + 4 Risikomanagement (+1 structural).

**The 20 top-level groups of the G++ catalog:** GC Governance und Compliance, STM Strukturmodellierung, UMS Umsetzung, VRB Verbesserung, PERF Monitoring-Evaluation, RISK Risikomanagement, ASST Informationen und Assets, PERS Personal, BES Beschaffungsmanagement, DLS Dienstleistersteuerung, TEST Änderungen und Tests, GEB Gebäudemanagement, SENS Sensibilisierung, ARCH Architektur, BER Berechtigung, NOT Notfallplanung, DET Detektion, REA Sicherheitsvorfallsbehandlung, KONF Konfiguration, DEV Entwicklung.

**Prop model per control (current):** `statement`, `modal_verb` (MUSS/SOLLTE/KANN, DIN 820-2/RFC 2119-based), `action_word`, `result`, `result_specification`, `sec_level` (`normal-SdT`/`erhöht`), `effort_level`, `guidance`, `documentation`, `tags`, `target_object_categories`, `label`, `alt-identifier`, plus since July: `confidentiality`/`integrity`/`availability`/`authenticity` (0–2) and `threats` (G 0.x) on all 901 Kernel-derived controls.

---

## Impact on our downstream work (from previous sessions)

- **Path breakage:** the 2026-07-27 restructure invalidated every raw-GitHub URL. We applied the path mapping across the Grundschutz-Plus-Plus-Tools repo on 2026-07-27 (246 files); PR #21 in the tools repo ("Adapt to restructured BSI Stand-der-Technik-Bibliothek + new stage_prozessbausteine", merged ~2026-07-31, https://github.com/NTT-Data-Deutschland-SE/Grundschutz-Plus-Plus-Tools/pull/21) redid the mapping cleanly, added `stage_prozessbausteine`, and updated published hrefs. *Note: this is a PR in the NTT Data tools repo, not in the SdT repo — the SdT repo's own PR #21 is an unrelated CI-workflow PR.*
- **Control-ID drift:** the June/July catalog consolidation dropped 63 control IDs referenced by our generated profiles. All 229 profiles were regenerated after PR #21; verified 2026-08-01 — zero stale IDs remain.
- **CIA props supersede our own:** since 2026-07-03 the BSI catalog carries authoritative per-control `confidentiality`/`integrity`/`availability`/`authenticity` props. Decision (2026-08-01): **SdT ist gesetzt** — our AI-generated `effective_on_c/i/a` props were removed everywhere (pipeline, schema, all 95 enhanced profiles); `ssp_ausfuellen.html` now renders the BSI props directly. G++-own props kept: `control_class`, `phase`, `label` (no BSI equivalent).
- **Namespace matching:** per-file ns URIs moved to `documentation/namespaces/` with renamed CSVs (`modal_verbs.csv`, `security_level.csv`). Matching props **by name** rather than by ns URI is the robust convention; `ssp_generator.html` was switched accordingly.
- **Prop stability:** verified 2026-08-01 — prop set and value enums identical between the 2026-07-17 and current catalogs (only the metadata prop `resolution-tool` was dropped). No new migration pressure at this time.

## Outlook

- The empty `assessment_layer/` and the "rolling publication" pipeline signal that assessment artifacts (SAP/SAR-side OSCAL) and more frequent automated releases are coming.
- The Mindeststandard-TLS draft is stale (April) and will likely be replaced through the rolling pipeline.
- Mapping collections (ISO 27001, IT-GS 2023) are new ground — worth watching as candidates for integration into the G++ tooling.
- **Control-ID stability is the open sore point**: two renumbering waves within one month, partially reversing each other (BER.7 → BER.6 → BER.7), with no changelog, no deprecation markers, and no stable alternative identifier for renumbered requirements. Anyone maintaining profiles, SSPs or mappings against the catalog has to re-diff on every release. This is the strongest candidate for an upstream issue.

---

Update: Changes since the report date (2026-08-01 to 2026-08-13)
 
**Period covered:** 2026-08-01 (report date above) to 2026-08-13
**Activity:** 1 merged PR: #86 "chore: publish rolling artifacts" (3 commits: `7346cf8` rolling artifacts, `d98237f` namespace definitions, `6627dc7` Grundschutz++ parameter resolution; merged 2026-08-13 as `6e70969`). No other commits landed on `main` in this period.
